hardwareFindings.title: Basalt engine, same Q4 weights
hardwareFindings.body: Basalt is an open-source (MIT) inference engine for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs; it runs a fixed list of models from its own converted .basalt packs. It runs the daily driver's Q4 weights at 282 tok/s vs 163 on llama.cpp; at 117k context 271 vs 99 tok/s, prefill about 10K vs 5K tok/s. Text core 96.0 vs 96.1 on llama.cpp. Real-repo fixes 96%, debugging 100%, long sessions 100%. Strata: 206 tok/s with DFlash2 drafting. The 27B on Basalt (its NVFP4 pack, RTX 5090): 193 vs 134 tok/s, text core 94.4 vs 92.8.

hardwareFindings.title: One model per GPU
hardwareFindings.body: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 on the PRO 6000 while the 5090 runs a second model: about 4% slower than alone.

hardwareFindings.title: One model across both GPUs
hardwareFindings.body: Layer split fits 200-320B models (GLM-5.3-Flash, MiMo, Step, Q5) but none beat the single-GPU Q4.

hardwareFindings.title: Both GPUs + system RAM
hardwareFindings.body: Bigger models whose experts spill into RAM run, but slowly: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 428B 22 tok/s, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 748B 17 tok/s and GLM-5.3 753B 12 tok/s, at best about 1/7 of the single-GPU Q4. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash scored 78.3 on its 24 core tasks.

hardwareFindings.title: Tensor parallel (-sm tensor)
hardwareFindings.body: Crashes on GLM-5.3-Flash in this llama.cpp build (unsupported tensor view); layer split only.

hardwareFindings.title: CPU only
hardwareFindings.body: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 16 Zen 5 cores: 157 tok/s prefill. The CPU's real job is hosting MoE experts.

hardwareFindings.title: Big lookup tables on SSD
hardwareFindings.body: DeepSeek-V4.1's 111 GB Engram table stays on NVMe (read one row per token): a 763B-class model on one GPU with ~8 GB of RAM.

hardwareFindings.title: Two NVMe drives in parallel
hardwareFindings.body: 3.7 + 3.6 GB/s for 2 MB random reads. Splitting a streamed model across both drives doubles read speed.

hardwareFindings.title: MTP speculative decoding
hardwareFindings.body: Built-in multi-token prediction: 104 tok/s without, 156-162 tok/s with draft length 2-4.

hardwareFindings.title: Windows commit limit
hardwareFindings.body: WDDM charges VRAM to system commit: a 90 GB model needs a large fixed pagefile, even with 128 GB of RAM.

verdict.en: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 on the RTX PRO 6000 is the daily driver: top-tier quality (96.1 text core; 7 local setups score inside the leader's 95% interval, with Flash-Next Q5, Qwen3.8-27B max, Flash-Next Q4 Basalt, Qwen3.8-27B Basalt, GLM-5.3-Flash Q2 and Qwen3.8-27B), fast (163 tok/s, 5.2 s per task; the only faster model in the top tier is Qwen3.8-27B Basalt), and it leaves the other GPU free for a second model. The same weights on the Basalt engine decode 1.7x faster at the same quality (text core 96.0, inside the pick's 95% interval; real-repo fixes, debugging and long sessions at least as good); this workstation has run it on Basalt since 26 Nov. Cloud references on the same tasks: Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) and GPT-6 Astra (max) score 96.7 (inside the local pick's 95% interval); the local pick is ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max), GPT-6.2 Sol (max) and Gemini 4 Hydrogen (xhigh).
verdict.zh: 主力：Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4，单卡 RTX PRO 6000。质量第一梯队（文本核心 96.1；有 7 个本地配置落在第一名的 95% 置信区间内，另外几个是 Flash-Next Q5、Qwen3.8-27B max、Flash-Next Q4 Basalt、Qwen3.8-27B Basalt、GLM-5.3-Flash Q2、Qwen3.8-27B），速度快（163 tok/s，单题 5.2 秒；第一梯队里比它快的其他模型只有 Qwen3.8-27B Basalt），另一张卡空出来跑第二个模型。同一套权重换 Basalt 引擎，解码快 1.7 倍，质量一样（文本核心 96.0，在主力的 95% 置信区间内；真实仓库修 bug、调试、长程都不比原来差），11 月 26 日起这台机器日常改用 Basalt。云端参照（同一套题）：Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh)、GPT-6 Astra (max) 96.7 分（在本地主力的 95% 置信区间内），本地主力高于 Claude Opus 5.5 (max)、GPT-6.2 Sol (max)、Gemini 4 Hydrogen (xhigh)。

headline.en: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 on the RTX PRO 6000 is the daily driver: top-tier quality (96.1 text core) and fast (163 tok/s). Since 26 Nov it runs on the Basalt engine: the same weights at 282 tok/s, 1.7× llama.cpp.
headline.zh: 主力：Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4，单卡 RTX PRO 6000，质量第一梯队（文本核心 96.1），速度快（163 tok/s）。11 月 26 日起改用 Basalt 引擎：同一套权重 282 tok/s，是 llama.cpp 的 1.7 倍。

title.zh: 11 月 26 日起的日常引擎：Basalt

text.en: Same weights: 282 tok/s (1.7× llama.cpp), 3.2 s per task, text core 96.0 vs 96.1; agentic results at least as good.
text.zh: 同一套权重：282 tok/s（llama.cpp 的 1.7 倍），单题 3.2 秒，文本核心 96.0 对 96.1，Agent 任务不比原来差。

about.en: Open-source (MIT), NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs only, and a fixed list of models in its own .basalt format. Audited here: it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, has no telemetry or update checks, and fetching URLs named in requests is turned off.
about.zh: 开源（MIT），只支持 NVIDIA Blackwell 显卡和它列出的几个模型，用自己的 .basalt 格式。已在本机审查：只监听 127.0.0.1，没有遥测，不检查更新；请求里的网址已设为不读取。

text.en: On the RTX 5090: 193 tok/s with Basalt's NVFP4 pack, text core 94.4, 3.7 s per task, 9/9 real-repo fixes.
text.zh: 放在 RTX 5090 上，用 Basalt 的 NVFP4 权重包：193 tok/s，文本核心 94.4，单题 3.7 秒，真实仓库修 bug 9/9。

title.en: Our max vs the cloud's max

text.en: Qwen3.8-27B xhigh 96.3 vs GPT-6 Astra max 96.7 (tied with Gemini 4 Neon xhigh): within noise. Behind on tool calling (−17), debugging (−10) and Chinese intent (−6); ahead on browser agent (+20).
text.zh: Qwen3.8-27B xhigh 96.3 对 GPT-6 Astra max 96.7（和 Gemini 4 Neon xhigh 并列），差距在误差内。落后：工具调用（−17）、调试（−10）、中文意图（−6）；领先：浏览器（+20）。

text.en: Asked about a 986K-token code dump, the Q4 got 14 of 20 questions right (32K to 1M: 100 / 100 / 99 / 99 / 77%; closed book 10%). 3 of the misses were right answers without the required answer line. Reading the dump took 7.0 min on both GPUs with YaRN ×4; follow-up questions 1.9 s. On Basalt, the daily engine, the same weights got 17 of 20 on the RTX PRO 6000 alone, read the dump in 2.4 min and decoded 256 tok/s.
text.zh: 给 Q4 一份 986K token 的代码，20 题答对 14 题（32K 到 1M：100 / 100 / 99 / 99 / 77%；不给代码只答对 10%）。其中 3 题其实答对了，只是没按要求写答案行。双卡加 YaRN ×4，读完整份要 7.0 分钟，之后每个追问 1.9 秒。日常用的 Basalt 引擎上，同一套权重只用 RTX PRO 6000 一张卡答对 17 题，读完整份 2.4 分钟，生成 256 tok/s。

title.zh: Q4 思考强度开高反而变差

text.en: Flash-Next Q4 at xhigh scored 86.5 vs 96.1 at medium; 2 answers hit the 64K-token cap. The 27B went the other way: 92.8 to 96.3.
text.zh: Flash-Next Q4 开到 xhigh 是 86.5 分，medium 是 96.1，有 2 道题写满了 64K token 上限。27B 正好相反：92.8 升到 96.3。

title.en: Giant models in system RAM: too slow
title.zh: 放进内存的超大模型：太慢

text.en: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 428B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 748B and GLM-5.3 753B decode 9–22 tok/s on both GPUs plus system RAM, at best about 1/7 of the Q4; the best score was MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's 78.3 on 24 tasks.
text.zh: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 428B、DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 748B、GLM-5.3 753B 放在两张卡加内存上只有 9–22 tok/s，最快也只有 Q4 的 1/7 左右；分数最高的 MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 是 78.3（24 题）。

methodology.title: Same tasks for every model
methodology.body: The headline score uses the first tasks of every suite (6 in most), intersected across models, so every model answers exactly the same 59 questions. Partial runs are scored on the subset they finished.

methodology.title: Text core = ranking metric
methodology.body: Mean of the 8 text suites' scores (vision excluded, so text-only models compete on equal terms). 95% confidence intervals come from a task-level bootstrap; overlapping intervals mean the gap is noise.

methodology.title: Graded by code, not by a judge model
methodology.body: Hidden unit tests, exact numeric answers, field-level JSON matching and real test suites. No LLM judge.

methodology.title: Agentic suites are separate
methodology.body: Real-repo bug fixes, debugging and long sessions run real tools in scratch clones with a sandbox that blocks network, child processes and writes outside the working copy. They are reported apart from the core score.

methodology.title: Long context to 1M tokens
methodology.body: One dump of real code per size (30K to 986K tokens) and the same 20 questions at every size, their answers at the same relative depths: look-ups, chains of constants planted far apart, and lists of tagged files (F1). A closed-book run of the same questions shows what guessing earns. A size runs only if the dump plus a fixed 16,384-token answer budget fits the setup's context, counted by the server's own tokenizer. Qwen3.8 models go past their trained 262K tokens with YaRN ×4.

methodology.title: Speed is measured on this PC
methodology.body: Decode = short prompts with the model's speculative decoding on; first output = median time until the first answer token or tool call of a core task, after any thinking; prefill and TTFT measured at 8K-117K tokens of context; task time = median wall time per core task, thinking included.

methodology.title: Private data stays private
methodology.body: The tasks come from the owner's real work, so only aggregate scores are published here: no prompts, answers, task ids, account or institution names.

methodology.title: Cloud references
methodology.body: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, Gemini 4 Neon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen answer the same tasks through the GitHub Copilot CLI at their highest reasoning effort (max; xhigh for Gemini, its top setting) with built-in tools off (published now: Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh), GPT-6 Astra (max), Claude Opus 5.5 (max), GPT-6.2 Sol (max), Gemini 4 Hydrogen (xhigh)). Each task's own tools are given to the model over MCP and run by the same harness and graders. They are references, not ranked with the local setups, and their speed is not comparable.

methodology.title: Our max vs their max
methodology.body: The comparison pits the best local result at the highest reasoning effort our models accept (Qwen3.8: xhigh) against the best cloud reference at its highest effort, suite by suite, on the same questions and graders. Local max runs get a 65,536-token output budget per reply (32,768 for the other local runs) so long xhigh reasoning isn't cut off; the cloud CLI sets its own.
